bull_bear.body: Debt-free; Rs.127cr reserves are advance against orders (not for buybacks/dividends); capex funded internally via cash flows; future funding only for major leaps in R&D or large-scale expansion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Intense domestic competition from unorganized players; potential entry of Chinese equipment manufacturers in solar segment; global supply chain disruptions for high-tech components; long order conversion cycles (8-9% pipeline-to-order rate); reliance on export demand volatility.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, and technology-focused; emphasis on differentiation over price wars; proud of first-mover status in solar; transparent about capacity constraints and future expansion plans; optimistic on import substitution trends.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite high order book (Rs.200cr+), management avoids 100% capacity utilization to maintain service agility — a strategic buffer uncommon in capital goods; solar opportunity is tiny in revenue today but strategically critical for long-term valuation re-rating as India pushes solar localization.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Fund-raising via Qualified Institutional Placement appears twice in the journey timeline: "Raising of funds through QIP up to Rs. 225 Crore" and "Company raised Rs. 160 Cr through Qualified Institutional Placement".
- Inorganic deployment: invested in a 60% majority stake in Kohli Printing and Converting Machines Pvt. Ltd., and signed an NBIO for a strategic acquisition in the machinery segment.
- Strategic investment of Rs. 300 mn in Yantralaya, alongside land acquisition (3 industrial plots; 80-acre park) — i.e. capital directed to capacity and capability rather than disclosed as shareholder returns.
- Deck reports key ratios on a consolidated basis with its own definitions: "RoE = Net Profit/Net Worth | RoA = Net Profit/Average Total Assets / RoCE = EBIT/(Shareholders Fund + Total Debt-non current investments)"; RoCE is shown at 20.3% in FY26 versus 32.5% in FY25, and RoE at 14.3% versus 23.3%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- technology: PROEX platform's RELEX 4.0 extruder engineered for 30% higher throughput with superior melt quality and energy efficiency — evidence: unveiled at K-2025, the world's largest plastics and rubber trade fair
- distribution: export reach across more than 70 countries — evidence: BRSR discloses exports to 45 countries contributing 51.65% of total turnover
- integration: acquisition of Kohli Printing and Converting Machines extends the company from extrusion into printing, coating, lamination and slitting, enabling integrated end-to-end solutions — evidence: 60% equity stake acquired September 2025, a 70-year-old precision printing/coating/laminating machine maker
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and trade flow risk — Ongoing geopolitical uncertainties impacted global trade flows during H2 FY26, leading to deferment of certain large export orders and elevated freight and logistics costs; both export and domestic markets were affected.
- Competition risk — The company faces competition from domestic and multinational players across each of its machinery segments, pressuring pricing and market share.
- Input cost risk — Profitability and cost effectiveness may be affected by changes in raw material prices, power availability and other input costs.
- Credit risk — Exposure to client payment risk on projects; the company manages this through credit limits, client financial health assessment and receivables follow-up.
- Interest rate risk — The company took on borrowings during FY26 (previously nil), introducing exposure to interest-rate movements even though leverage remains conservative.
- Liability risk — Risk of liability arising from damage to cargo, equipment, life or third parties, mitigated through contractual obligations and insurance.
- Regulatory and sustainability risk — Increasingly stringent environmental regulations (EU Single-Use Plastics Directive, EPR mandates, recycled-content requirements, upcoming digital product passport regime) require continuous adaptation in machinery design.
- Export and geographic concentration — Exports contribute 51.65% of total turnover across 45 countries, exposing the company to freight, logistics and cross-border trade disruptions.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Flexible Packaging Machinery: 70-75% of revenue (export-heavy); Solar Encapsulation Film Systems: nascent, Rs.20-25cr expected over next 2 years; PVC/CPVC Lines: 33% installed capacity share in India; Agriculture/Pharma: minor but growing segments.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Described as "Among leading extrusion machinery manufacturers" with "Over three decades excellence in extrusion" and a record of "technology firsts" plus the ability to suit solutions to regional needs.
- Company snapshot claims 40+ years of excellence in manufacturing extrusion machineries, 52+ years of promoter experience, 5K+ installations, exports to 70+ countries and 26+ products across 6 different segments.
- Claims to be the "Only Company in India to offer most 'energy efficient' products", and cites strong customer loyalty with "~60% of business, every year generated through repeat orders" from marquee names including Uflex, Reliance Industries, Indian Oil, Binny Wads, Suvi International, Synthetic Packaging, Abhinav Industries and S D International.
- Key strategic partnerships listed are Bausano & Figli (Italy), MEAF Machines B.V. (Netherlands) and Wonderpack (Nashik, India); geographical footprint spans Latin America, Europe, North & South America, Gulf/Middle East, East, Northeast, West and Southern Africa, Asia Pacific and Australia.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Invests in 60% majority stake in Kohli Printing and Converting Machines Pvt. Ltd.; separately, a "High Impact Alliance between Rajoo Engineers and Kohli Industries to Change Market Dynamics of Extrusion Coating & Lamination Machines" is listed in the earlier journey period.
- [JV] Historic JV with Bausano of Italy in the plastic pipe manufacturing industry, plus a Wonderpack merger for the benefit of the thermoforming industry and technical collaborations with Commodore Inc. U.S.A. (Tekni-Plex Inc.) for XPS sheet line and Hosokawa Alpine, Germany for blown film line.
- [Industry structure] India's plastics processing machinery market is stated to be growing @ 8.5% over the last 4 years, with 20+ major machinery manufacturers and 300+ small & medium manufacturers, and processing machinery exported to over 50 countries (Source: Industry Estimate / PMMAI).
- [Industry data] Extrusion machine installations in India rose from 2,950 units (2018-19) to 5,330 units (2024-25), a stated 7-year CAGR of 10.4%, with extrusion investment of INR 6,880 crore in 2024-25 at a stated 15.8% CAGR (Source: Plastindia Foundation / Industry Estimate / IBEF).
- [Order wins] Journey timeline records receipt of a high-value order of Rs. 31 Crs from Europe, and a high-value order of 137 Crore alongside an achieved export order of Rs. 106 Cr.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Rajoo Engineers manufactures plastic extrusion machinery — blown film, thermoforming and sheet extrusion lines — sold directly to Indian and overseas customers through its own sales and marketing team. Its customer base spans packaging, infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, consumer goods and other industrial applications, and the company markets and services this machinery with an emphasis on long-term customer relationships and after-sales support.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin: 16.1% (Q2), 15.1% (H1) up 270-320 bps YoY; PAT margin: 12.7% (Q2), 11.7% (H1); raw material prices stable but tech upgrades increase input cost complexity; margin expansion driven by higher-value product mix and operational efficiency, not cost-cutting.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Sustainable revenue growth of 12-15% annually; EBITDA margin expansion of 2-3% through standardization and operational efficiency; no dividend policy mentioned; focus on high-value product mix.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Solar encapsulation film extrusion systems (first-mover in India); potential for export expansion into Southeast Asia and Africa; consolidation of land bank (30,000 sq.ft) for future capacity expansion; possible entry into pharmaceutical packaging machinery.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Accelerate the integration of Kohli Printing and Converting Machines to realise synergies across the flexible packaging value chain.
- Optimise product mix toward higher-margin, value-added offerings.
- Continue investing in R&D to extend technology leadership.
- Strengthen the export pipeline as global markets normalise.
- Pursue portfolio diversification through the newly launched Panel Division.
- Pursue opportunistic inorganic growth using the QIP-raised capital as "dry powder".
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Rajoo completed a major technology upgrade at its Shree Yantralaya machine shop, installing an Okuma Multus advanced multi-tasking machine from Japan and adding multitasking, vertical turning, milling and high-performance machining capabilities in-house. The company acquired a 60% stake in Kohli Printing and Converting Machines Private Limited in September 2025, extending its capabilities into printing, coating, laminating and slitting technologies alongside its extrusion business. Rajoo also launched a new Panel Division to expand its product and technology portfolio into panel solutions, targeting domestic and international markets.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural demand outlook for extrusion machinery is described as compelling across flexible packaging, agriculture, infrastructure, electronics, healthcare and renewable energy.
- Near-term headwinds flagged: raw material cost volatility, elevated logistics and freight costs, and geopolitical uncertainties.
- Achievements supported by robust demand, improved operational efficiencies and healthy order inflows across customers in more than 70 countries.
- Company describes a "strong consolidated order pipeline" as of the Chairman's letter for FY26.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

summary.oneLiner: Rajoo Engineers Limited is an Indian manufacturer of plastic extrusion plant and machinery, covering blown film, thermoforming and sheet extrusion, serving customers across more than 70 countries.
summary.business: Rajoo Engineers manufactures plastic extrusion machinery — blown film, thermoforming and sheet extrusion lines — sold directly to Indian and overseas customers through its own sales and marketing team. Its customer base spans packaging, infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, consumer goods and other industrial applications, and the company markets and services this machinery with an emphasis on long-term customer relationships and after-sales support.

Rajoo also launched a new Panel Division to expand its product and technology portfolio into panel solutions, …

one-line thesis: Rajoo Engineers is a dominant Indian capital goods player in flexible packaging machinery with strong export exposure, now leveraging first-mover advantage in solar encapsulation film extrusion systems to capture import-substitution opportunities, while maintaining high margins through technology differentiation and debt-free balance sheet.
financial scorecard: rev: +27.07% YoY (H1); EBITDA: +61.23% YoY (H1); PAT: +62.27% YoY (H1); orderbook: Rs.200cr+; netdebt: debt-free
guidance: Sustainable revenue growth of 12-15% annually; EBITDA margin expansion of 2-3% through standardization and operational efficiency; no dividend policy mentioned; focus on high-value product mix.
segment / subsidiary detail: Flexible Packaging Machinery: 70-75% of revenue (export-heavy); Solar Encapsulation Film Systems: nascent, Rs.20-25cr expected over next 2 years; PVC/CPVC Lines: 33% installed capacity share in India; Agriculture/Pharma: minor but growing segments.
growth verticals / optionality: Solar encapsulation film extrusion systems (first-mover in India); potential for export expansion into Southeast Asia and Africa; consolidation of land bank (30,000 sq.ft) for future capacity expansion; possible entry into pharmaceutical packaging machinery.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin: 16.1% (Q2), 15.1% (H1) up 270-320 bps YoY; PAT margin: 12.7% (Q2), 11.7% (H1); raw material prices stable but tech upgrades increase input cost complexity; margin expansion driven by higher-value product mix and operational efficiency, not cost-cutting.
capex / expansion: Rs.100cr+ invested in FY25 (Rajkot facility expansion: 18,000 sq.ft assembly + 7,000 sq.ft QA; tooling & machining center; 3 land plots acquired); next capex cycle expected in FY26.
capital allocation: Debt-free; Rs.127cr reserves are advance against orders (not for buybacks/dividends); capex funded internally via cash flows; future funding only for major leaps in R&D or large-scale expansion.
risks & watch-items: Intense domestic competition from unorganized players; potential entry of Chinese equipment manufacturers in solar segment; global supply chain disruptions for high-tech components; long order conversion cycles (8-9% pipeline-to-order rate); reliance on export demand volatility.
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, and technology-focused; emphasis on differentiation over price wars; proud of first-mover status in solar; transparent about capacity constraints and future expansion plans; optimistic on import substitution trends.
non-obvious takeaways: Despite high order book (Rs.200cr+), management avoids 100% capacity utilization to maintain service agility — a strategic buffer uncommon in capital goods; solar opportunity is tiny in revenue today but strategically critical for long-term valuation re-rating as India pushes solar localization.

Its customer base spans packaging, infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, consumer goods and other industrial applications, and the company markets and services this machinery with an emphasis on long-term customer relationships and after-sales support.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Sustainable revenue growth of 12-15% annually; EBITDA margin expansion of 2-3% through standardization and operational efficiency; no dividend policy mentioned; focus on high-value product mix.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Solar encapsulation film extrusion systems (first-mover in India); potential for export expansion into Southeast Asia and Africa; consolidation of land bank (30,000 sq.ft) for future capacity expansion; possible entry into pharmaceutical packaging machinery.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural demand outlook for extrusion machinery is described as compelling across flexible packaging, agriculture, infrastructure, electronics, healthcare and renewable energy.
- Near-term headwinds flagged: raw material cost volatility, elevated logistics and freight costs, and geopolitical uncertainties.
- Achievements supported by robust demand, improved operational efficiencies and healthy order inflows across customers in more than 70 countries.
- Company describes a "strong consolidated order pipeline" as of the Chairman's letter for FY26.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin: 16.1% (Q2), 15.1% (H1) up 270-320 bps YoY; PAT margin: 12.7% (Q2), 11.7% (H1); raw material prices stable but tech upgrades increase input cost complexity; margin expansion driven by higher-value product mix and operational efficiency, not cost-cutting.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt-free; Rs.127cr reserves are advance against orders (not for buybacks/dividends); capex funded internally via cash flows; future funding only for major leaps in R&D or large-scale expansion.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Rajoo completed a major technology upgrade at its Shree Yantralaya machine shop, installing an Okuma Multus advanced multi-tasking machine from Japan and adding multitasking, vertical turning, milling and high-performance machining capabilities in-house. The company acquired a 60% stake in Kohli Printing and Converting Machines Private Limited in September 2025, extending its capabilities into printing, coating, laminating and slitting technologies alongside its extrusion business. Rajoo also launched a new Panel Division to expand its product and technology portfolio into panel solutions, targeting domestic and international markets.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, strategic, and technology-focused; emphasis on differentiation over price wars; proud of first-mover status in solar; transparent about capacity constraints and future expansion plans; optimistic on import substitution trends.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- technology: PROEX platform's RELEX 4.0 extruder engineered for 30% higher throughput with superior melt quality and energy efficiency — evidence: unveiled at K-2025, the world's largest plastics and rubber trade fair
- distribution: export reach across more than 70 countries — evidence: BRSR discloses exports to 45 countries contributing 51.65% of total turnover
- integration: acquisition of Kohli Printing and Converting Machines extends the company from extrusion into printing, coating, lamination and slitting, enabling integrated end-to-end solutions — evidence: 60% equity stake acquired September 2025, a 70-year-old precision printing/coating/laminating machine maker

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Intense domestic competition from unorganized players; potential entry of Chinese equipment manufacturers in solar segment; global supply chain disruptions for high-tech components; long order conversion cycles (8-9% pipeline-to-order rate); reliance on export demand volatility.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Despite high order book (Rs.200cr+), management avoids 100% capacity utilization to maintain service agility — a strategic buffer uncommon in capital goods; solar opportunity is tiny in revenue today but strategically critical for long-term valuation re-rating as India pushes solar localization.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Accelerate the integration of Kohli Printing and Converting Machines to realise synergies across the flexible packaging value chain.
- Optimise product mix toward higher-margin, value-added offerings.
- Continue investing in R&D to extend technology leadership.
- Strengthen the export pipeline as global markets normalise.
- Pursue portfolio diversification through the newly launched Panel Division.
- Pursue opportunistic inorganic growth using the QIP-raised capital as "dry powder".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Invests in 60% majority stake in Kohli Printing and Converting Machines Pvt. Ltd.; separately, a "High Impact Alliance between Rajoo Engineers and Kohli Industries to Change Market Dynamics of Extrusion Coating & Lamination Machines" is listed in the earlier journey period.
- [JV] Historic JV with Bausano of Italy in the plastic pipe manufacturing industry, plus a Wonderpack merger for the benefit of the thermoforming industry and technical collaborations with Commodore Inc. U.S.A. (Tekni-Plex Inc.) for XPS sheet line and Hosokawa Alpine, Germany for blown film line.
- [Industry structure] India's plastics processing machinery market is stated to be growing @ 8.5% over the last 4 years, with 20+ major machinery manufacturers and 300+ small & medium manufacturers, and processing machinery exported to over 50 countries (Source: Industry Estimate / PMMAI).
- [Industry data] Extrusion machine installations in India rose from 2,950 units (2018-19) to 5,330 units (2024-25), a stated 7-year CAGR of 10.4%, with extrusion investment of INR 6,880 crore in 2024-25 at a stated 15.8% CAGR (Source: Plastindia Foundation / Industry Estimate / IBEF).
- [Order wins] Journey timeline records receipt of a high-value order of Rs. 31 Crs from Europe, and a high-value order of 137 Crore alongside an achieved export order of Rs. 106 Cr.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.
